data.case1.title: Digital Training Program
data.case1.description: Technology training program for youth from vulnerable communities, focusing on programming, design, and digital entrepreneurship.
data.case1.challenge: Low employability and income among youth aged 18-29 in peripheral areas, with only 23% finding formal employment after high school.
data.case1.solution: IMPACT7 methodology applied for market competency-based curriculum design, participant selection by transformation potential, and continuous measurement of results with real-time adjustments.
data.case1.results: 12.4x social return on investment, with 87% of graduates employed within 6 months and an average 180% increase in family income.
data.case1.testimonial.quote: The program changed my life. I went from an informal job earning R$ 800 to a junior developer position with R$ 4,500. Now I can help my family and have a future perspective.
data.case1.testimonial.author: Maria Santos
data.case2.title: Solidarity Microcredit Network
data.case2.description: Microcredit program with technical support for low-income entrepreneurs, combining capital with management training.
data.case2.challenge: Lack of access to formal credit and management knowledge for small entrepreneurs in low-income communities, with 78% depending on loan sharks.
data.case2.solution: Combination of microcredit with fair rates, personalized mentoring, and financial management training, using the IMPACT7 methodology to identify entrepreneurs with the highest growth potential.
data.case2.results: 2,400 new businesses created, with a default rate of only 3.2% (vs. 15% market average) and an average 220% increase in family income.
data.case2.testimonial.quote: With the microcredit and mentoring, I was able to transform my fruit stand into a small grocery store. Today I employ 3 people from the community.
data.case2.testimonial.author: José Ferreira
data.case3.title: Community Preventive Health
data.case3.description: Chronic disease prevention program through community health agents equipped with mobile technology.
data.case3.challenge: High incidence of preventable chronic diseases in low-income communities, with 67% of residents without regular medical follow-up.
data.case3.solution: Network of 120 community agents with mobile app for health monitoring and education, using IMPACT7 to prioritize highest-impact interventions.
data.case3.results: 4,200 hospitalizations avoided, generating R$ 12M savings for the public health system and 94% increase in vaccination coverage.
data.case3.testimonial.quote: The health agents helped me control my diabetes. Before I went to the hospital every month, now I do follow-up at home and don't need hospitalization anymore.
data.case3.testimonial.author: Mrs. Maria Aparecida
data.case4.title: Sustainable Family Farming
data.case4.description: Transition program to organic farming with technical assistance and market access for small rural producers.
data.case4.challenge: Low productivity and income of family farmers, with 45% living below the poverty line and intensive use of pesticides.
data.case4.solution: Training in agroecological techniques, collective organic certification, and direct connection with consumer markets through cooperative.
data.case4.results: 156% increase in productivity, 340 families certified as organic, and access to premium markets with 40% higher prices.
data.case4.testimonial.quote: I stopped using poison on my crops and now I earn more selling organic. My children want to continue on the land, something they never thought about before.
data.case4.testimonial.author: João da Silva
data.case5.title: Integrated Social Housing
data.case5.description: Slum urbanization program with housing construction, land regularization, and integrated community development.
data.case5.challenge: 700 families living in risk areas with precarious housing, without basic sanitation and without property titles.
data.case5.solution: Integrated urbanization with community participation, using IMPACT7 to prioritize interventions and measure multidimensional impact.
data.case5.results: 700 families with decent housing and property titles, average 280% property appreciation, and 95% reduction in sanitation-related diseases.
data.case5.testimonial.quote: I lived 30 years in a wooden shack. Today I have a brick house with my name on the deed. My grandchildren will inherit something of value.
data.case5.testimonial.author: Mr. Antônio
data.case6.title: Digital Inclusion for Seniors
data.case6.description: Digital literacy program for seniors focusing on autonomy, social connection, and access to online public services.
data.case6.challenge: 85% of seniors over 65 without basic digital skills, resulting in service exclusion and social isolation.
data.case6.solution: Methodology adapted for seniors with in-person classes, simplified teaching materials, and support from young volunteers.
data.case6.results: 4,800 seniors digitally literate, 62% reduction in social isolation rates, and 340% increase in access to online services.
data.case6.testimonial.quote: I learned to video call my grandchildren who live far away. Now I also schedule medical appointments on my phone. I feel part of the world again.
data.case6.testimonial.author: Mrs. Irene

math.title: The Mathematics of Impact
math.subtitle: Understand the equation that quantifies social transformation potential and how each variable influences the result.

equation.title: The Fundamental Equation
equation.description: Impact (I) is directly proportional to invested Energy (E) multiplied by Context (C) raised to the seventh power, and inversely proportional to Resistance (R).

variables.title: The Equation Variables
variables.subtitle: Each variable represents a fundamental aspect of the social project

I.name: Impact
I.description: Measurable result of the social intervention

E.name: Energy (Investment)
E.description: Sum of all resources invested in the project

C.name: Context
C.description: Degree of alignment with the 7 contextual dimensions

R.name: Resistance
R.description: Sum of barriers and frictions that reduce impact

powerOf7.title: Why C⁷?
powerOf7.subtitle: The exponent 7 is not arbitrary. It represents the 7 contextual dimensions that, when aligned, generate an exponential multiplier effect on impact.

1.name: Cultural
1.description: Alignment with local values and practices

effect.title: Exponential Effect
effect.description: When C = 0.5, C⁷ = 0.0078 (greatly reduced impact). When C = 0.9, C⁷ = 0.478 (significant impact). An increase from 0.5 to 0.9 in context results in a 61x increase in the multiplier!

sroi.title: S-ROI: Social Return on Investment
sroi.subtitle: The metric that translates impact into comparable value

socialValue.title: SV (Social Value)
socialValue.description: Sum of social benefits generated, monetized through validated proxies (e.g., avoided costs, generated productivity, increased well-being).

investment.title: E (Energy/Investment)
investment.description: Sum of all invested resources: financial, human, material, and technological.

interpretation.title: Interpretation
interpretation.description: An S-ROI of 7x means that for every $1 invested, $7 in social value is generated. The minimum benchmark recommended by the IMPACT7 Method is 7x.
